# Tobit Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_012_page_001.jpg

---

**12:1** Then Tobit-the-father called Tobias his-son and said to him, "See, my-child, to give the-wage to the-man who went with you, and to add to him [something] beyond [the wage]."

**12:2** And he said, "Father, how much shall-I give him as-a-wage? It will-not-harm [me] to-give him half of the-things he-brought with me;

**12:3** for he-led me in-safety, and he-healed my-wife, and the-silver he-brought with me, and he-healed you also."

**12:4** And the-old-man said, "It-is-fitting for him to-receive half of all the-things he-brought."

**12:5** And he-called him and said, "Take half of all the-things you-brought, and-go in-health."

**12:6** Then he-called them both privately and said to-them, "Bless the-God and give thanks before all-the-living for the-good-things he-did for you, so-that they-may bless and sing-praise to his-name. The-words of God make-known gloriously, and do-not-be-negligent in-thanking him.

**12:7** The-secret of a-king [it is] good to-hide, but the-works of God to-reveal gloriously [and] to-praise. Do the-good [thing], and evil will-not-find you.

**12:8** Good [is] prayer with fasting and eleēmosyna [almsgiving] and righteousness. A-little with righteousness [is] better than much with unrighteousness. [It is] better to-give eleēmosyna than to-lay-up gold.

**12:9** For eleēmosyna from death delivers and it-purges away every sin. Those-who-do eleēmosyna and righteousness will-be-filled with-life;

**12:10** but those-who-sin are enemies of their-own life.

**12:11** "I-will-not-hide then the-truth from you. I-have-said and I-have-hidden: [it is] good to-hide the-secret of a-king, but the-works of God to-reveal gloriously.

**12:12** And so when you-prayed and Sarah your-daughter-in-law, I-brought the-memorial of your-prayer before the-Holy-One; and when you-were-burying the-dead,

**12:13** and when you-left your-meal and went and-wrapped the-dead man, I-was-sent to-put-you-to-the-test.

**12:14** And at-the-same-time God sent me to-heal you and Sarah your-daughter-in-law.

**12:15** I am Raphael, one of the-seven holy-angels who-present the-prayers of the-holy-ones and enter before the-Glory of the-Holy-One."

**12:16** And they-were-troubled both of-them, and they-fell upon their-faces, for they-were-afraid.

**12:17** And he-said to-them, "Do-not-fear; peace be-to-you. Bless the-God through all the-ages.

**12:18** For not of my-[own] grace did-I come to-you, but by-the-will of our God. Therefore bless him through all the-days; to-him sing-praise.

**12:19** "And you-were-seeing me eating, but it-was a-vision you-were-seeing.

**12:20** And now give-thanks to-God, for I-am-ascending to-the-one-who-sent me. And write in-a-scroll all the-things that-happened."

**12:21** And they-rose up, and they-were-no-longer-able to-see him.

**12:22** And they-kept-blessing God and they-were-hymning him; and they-gave-thanks to-God for these great works of-his: [because] a-messenger of God appeared to-them.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

The pivotal verse of the book is 12:15. The Greek reads: *Egō eimi Raphael, heis tōn hepta angelōn tōn hagiōn hoi paristanousin kai eiserchonotai enōpion tēs doxēs tou Hagiou.* I have rendered *angelōn hagiōn* as "holy-angels" (hyphenated construct) and *enōpion tēs doxēs* as "before the-Glory," preserving the indirect divine reference — God is present as "the Glory of the Holy One," a reverential circumlocution.

*Eleēmosyna* (vv. 8–9) is preserved in transliteration throughout; it encompasses charitable giving, acts of mercy, and covenant-loyalty simultaneously — no English word captures all three. The LXX usage here is a terminus technicus for the virtue that averts divine judgment.

Verse 19: *horama* = "vision" — Raphael clarifies that his apparent eating was not literal consumption but a theophanic appearance. The word-for-word rendering preserves the theological precision.

Verse 7: *mystērion basileōs* = "secret of a-king" — this is a proverbial saying the angel uses as a foil to make his theological point about proclaiming God's works.

— EMET
